Gloomy Eyes
& The Last Standing

Avatars

The eight bodies you and your friends step into.

Eight of you

One body per guest. No two the same. Up to ten zombies can share a scene, often fewer.

Glowing and see-through

In most scenes the bodies glow and turn translucent, so a friend standing in front of you is never a wall. The group can cluster, cross and stand in your eyeline without ever stealing the shot.

how much of a body you see is chosen shot by shot

Full body, head and arms, or hands

Sometimes the whole body. Sometimes only a face and two hands. Sometimes just your own hands, entering from below the frame.

The rabbit disguise

In some scenes the avatars pull pale rabbit robes over the same dead body, long ears and two dark eye holes, to pass unseen among the living. It is how the group slips through moments a zombie would be caught, the train among them.

a form of its own

The Taiwanese zombie

A jiangshi: Qing-era robes, a paper talisman across the brow, arms locked forward, moving in stiff hops. It stands apart from the eight, a character all its own.

Eight avatars. Glowing, see-through, and no two the same.
